title: WordPress 7.1.5 Security Release Fixes 19 Vulnerabilities
content_md: WordPress 7.1.5 is a security release, and site owners should update immediately. 19 distinct vulnerabilities are tracked by Wordfence, including one Critical and four High-severity issues based on CVSS v3.1. Notable issues include an unauthenticated privilege escalation that could lead to remote code execution, SQL injection, stored cross-site scripting, XML-RPC denial of service, and a multisite Administrator-to-Super-Administrator privilege escalation. Eight vulnerabilities do not require authentication to exploit. However, several have additional prerequisites or require user interaction, so they are not universally exploitable on every WordPress site. WordPress 7.1.5 was released on November 18, 2026, with fixes for a broad group of security issues affecting WordPress Core. The release addresses privilege escalation, cross-site scripting, SQL injection, information disclosure, authorization bypass, cross-site request forgery, and denial of service. WordPress recommends updating immediately. Most sites with automatic background updates enabled will begin receiving the release automatically, but site owners should still confirm that the update completed.
